<a id="delivery-goal"></a>

## 3. Delivery Goal

Owner complexity direction on2026-10-23: native components should remain comparable in complexity to their canonical React components unless a concrete native requirement justifies more. Compare the actual reachable component behavior, including what its dependencies supply, rather than wrapper line counts alone. Prefer existing component primitives and scoped platform adapters; additional infrastructure must address a demonstrated component requirement. The unfinished field-input SDK prototype remains preserved while its approach is reassessed. This direction does not remove accepted capabilities, change the53-ID/477-cell finish line or count private construction as public delivery.

Status: **Active: complete M2 against the acceptance rubric and matrices below for all53 catalogue IDs.** On2026-10-17 Gabriel rejects the two-component finish line and requires completion conditions tied directly to precise acceptance rubrics and matrices. LinearProgress/Meter is a source checkpoint, not completion of this goal. Public native root coverage is53/53 at1bcfef4f; the acceptance matrix has0/53 fully closed rows and185 PASS/288 OPEN/one FAIL/three BLOCKED cells. Gabriel explicitly requests transfer and resumption after the53-source explanation, so final source/evidence work is active again; product and native attempts retain their separate approval boundaries. All unfinished construction and unresolved mandatory cells remain in scope. No component, batch, commit count, test count or wall-clock interval ends this goal.

Execute in dependency order on `feature/<description>` branches under §9.1, committing coherent contract/evidence, component/test and consumer/reference steps. Before each family, read its complete canonical source, inherited types/behavior and suites, then instantiate the exact capability/scenario rows and expected outcomes. Preserve controlled values, existing pins/palette, package ownership, sealed evidence, normal hooks and local Git identity. Use the established shared TypeScript/native style/state/ref/overlay patterns. Consolidate novel API/architecture/dependency/theme/registry/tooling decisions for owner review and continue unaffected rows while those decisions are pending. Branch pushes and library PR creation are authorized under §9.1. Merge, publication, workflow/distribution modifications, sibling edits and iPhone signing remain unauthorized.

The finish line is every applicable acceptance cell in sections [3.1.1–3.1.9](#31-acceptance-rubric), including the installed Android/iOS matrices. Stable `CAT.<manifest-id>.G01`–`G09` keys identify evidence cells only. The [evidence matrix](experiments.md#3-catalogue-acceptance-matrix) records the individual cells and proof links. `OPEN` means not yet reconciled or executed, not a failed test; `FAIL` and `BLOCKED` remain unresolved. A source/mock pass cannot close an installed cell. An agent-authored exclusion, a merely passing repeat or a diagnostic receipt cannot close a required cell. `N/A` needs the canonical-contract reason; `OWNER-DEFERRED` needs the exact existing/new owner authority and remains visibly deferred rather than passing. Existing physical/ARM/owner-visual deferrals are retained, not widened to emulator/simulator acceptance.

RN-TEXT-01 and original ComboBox failures keep their identities. They stop dependent installed/query propagation, not independent catalogue construction. Do not conduct further XCTest/LLDB/startup investigations while independent mandatory construction work remains. A later lab repair requires a materially new hypothesis and one goal-wide bounded attempt; repeated unchanged timeout investigations do not restart the workstream. If a required cell is externally blocked, preserve it, move to another incomplete cell and keep the goal incomplete. Exhausting all independently actionable work produces an explicit blocking decision, not a claim of completion.

<a id="acceptance-rubric"></a>

### 3.1. Acceptance Rubric

These rows operationalize the canonical web assertion baseline, existing native contracts, historical ledger Section 7.1–7.3 at `db54a8a`, Select's approved contract/installed matrix and searchable-selection priority gate. Their historical source paths and revisions remain in [the lookup](experiments.md#12-historical-document-lookup). They do not silently reapprove a deferred web capability. A new family instantiates row IDs before implementation; the ledger identifies the exact assertion/scenario and its verifier, revision, expected output and observed result.

<a id="canonical-capability-and-contract"></a>

#### 3.1.1. Canonical Capability And Contract

Evidence key: `G01`.

**Pass condition:** Enumerate every owned and inherited prop/default, state axis, callback/order/veto, ref/event, slot, geometry/size/color/order, keyboard/collection/formatting behavior and every assertion in the complete canonical web suites. Give each a native equivalent or an explicit owner-approved exclusion. No ignored prop or unreviewed exception.

**Closing evidence:** `CAP.<manifest-id>.<n>` rows naming canonical symbol/assertion, native contract/call site and expected outcome; approved decision reference for deviations. Every capability row must be dispositioned; merely linking a root suite is insufficient.

<a id="ownership-and-behavior"></a>

#### 3.1.2. Ownership And Behavior

Evidence key: `G02`.

**Pass condition:** Apply scenarios 3.2.1–3.2.6 to every supported state axis and action. Explicit false/0/empty string/empty array/contract-defined null remain distinct from undefined. Controlled requests wait for owner echo; repeated owner vetoes never mutate authoritative output. Defaults initialize once, callback order/count/guards remain correct, and removal/reinsertion/teardown produces no fabricated change.

**Closing evidence:** Named public-outcome tests with positive/negative requests, controlled/default transitions and exact callback traces. Add installed evidence wherever the observable behavior depends on native input, presentation, keyboard or gesture delivery.

<a id="executable-public-boundary"></a>

#### 3.1.3. Executable Public Boundary

Evidence key: `G03`.

**Pass condition:** Export only implemented props/types/constants; preserve native refs, identity/name precedence and original allowed event payloads. Require/validate names under the accepted contract, consume wrapper props and prevent aliases/child props from replacing owned values or handlers. Unsupported DOM/ownership surfaces fail executable public types.

**Closing evidence:** Positive/negative public call sites, native contract typecheck and compiled declarations, ref/native-event/host-prop assertions. Tests must actually fail for rejected cases rather than contain unused error directives.

<a id="customization-and-theme"></a>

#### 3.1.4. Customization And Theme

Evidence key: `G04`.

**Pass condition:** Cover every canonical geometry, size, order, mode, state and named style/content/icon slot. Both theme modes and mounted provider changes preserve current values. Computed → customStyles → final style and post-custom callback defaultStyle hold independently per owner; native dynamic colors and registered/array styles work and unsupported colors reject. Scaling stays enabled unless explicitly constrained.

**Closing evidence:** `STYLE.<manifest-id>.<n>` assertion mapping for every canonical customization assertion, native slot/state assertions and affected installed scenario 3.2.7–3.2.10 captures/measurements. No source/pixel equivalence inferred from object equality.

<a id="source-and-composition"></a>

#### 3.1.5. Source And Composition

Evidence key: `G05`.

**Pass condition:** Focused source and maintained-scene tests exercise actual public components/providers with host-owned state, including interaction, reset, live theme/window/fixture changes and async replacement as applicable. Mock only native/external seams; no snapshot or implementation-mirroring test substitutes for public behavior. Resolve attributed regressions.

**Closing evidence:** Exact named test cases/commands and source revision; passing focused suites, owning format/lint/type gates, app composition checks and meaningful negative cases. Unrelated broad suites are not rerun without invalidation.

<a id="immutable-consumer-and-build"></a>

#### 3.1.6. Immutable Consumer And Build

Evidence key: `G06`.

**Pass condition:** Build/pack the changed native package; freeze a fresh outside-workspace consumer using only its archive and declared host peers. Frozen reinstall and strict consumer types pass. Both Metro platform bundles/maps resolve to the recorded archive/fixture with no workspace/sibling source links, duplicate React or unintended DOM/web/runtime dependencies.

**Closing evidence:** Source/file hashes, archive SHA, package/lock/peer identities, consumer location and commands, iOS/Android bundle/map module assertions and exact compiled public exports. Older proof is reused only after the relevant byte/scope identity is verified.

<a id="installed-android"></a>

#### 3.1.7. Installed Android

Evidence key: `G07`.

**Pass condition:** Every applicable scenario in 3.2.1–3.2.12 passes on actual installed Release output across profiles 3.3.1–3.3.8. Record native callback/owner agreement, first activation and measured geometry/keyboard/window postconditions; preserve failed first attempts and attributable fixes.

**Closing evidence:** Android cell records source/archive/bundle/map/built/installed hashes, app/build ID, emulator/runtime/window/fontScale/theme, exact fixture/inspector, expected versus observed callbacks/frames and capture/log locations. A successful build or mock does not pass this gate.

<a id="installed-ios"></a>

#### 3.1.8. Installed iOS

Evidence key: `G08`.

**Pass condition:** The same applicable scenario 3.2.1–3.2.12/profile 3.3.1–3.3.8 matrix passes on the approved x86_64 simulator Release lane. Real observer callbacks are required before interpreting an editor/interaction verdict; healthy process/control handshakes are insufficient. Preserve exact first/warm conditions and immutable failure cohorts.

**Closing evidence:** iOS identities and evidence fields matching section 3.1.7, with observer/method/callback proof. Actual failed/blocked cells remain open even when unrelated cells or a repeated query pass. iPhone signing/ARM/physical proof is excluded only under the existing owner deferral.

<a id="review-and-docs-and-closure"></a>

#### 3.1.9. Review, Documentation And Closure

Evidence key: `G09`.

**Pass condition:** Resolve technical findings for the reviewed revision, document public use and explicit native equivalents/limits, maintain the scene and catalogue/matrix, and commit coherent changes through normal hooks. No unresolved mandatory capability or installed cell is promoted as accepted.

**Closing evidence:** Recorded technical review scope/revision/findings/resolution, current curated reference/scene, passing affected docs build and normal commit checks, clean/understood Git state, and a cell-by-cell completion audit. Physical/owner-visual deferrals stay linked to their authority.

<a id="execution-queue-and-approval-boundary"></a>

### 3.4. Execution Queue And Approval Boundary

Dependency-ready construction proceeds across visual/content/media primitives, selection/tags/toggles, progress/loaders/counter/form composition, range controls, links/navigation/feedback, overlay/menu/panel, tables, searchable multi-selection and date/time families. Audit each family rather than preselect a headless dependency. Existing source components also receive missing capability/assertion mappings and affected acceptance work. Novel navigation/overlay/collection/date semantics or dependency/theme/tooling changes require a concrete decision, while unrelated rows continue. Component contracts and results live here and in experiments.md; do not create another proposal/receipt document for each family.

###### 3.5.3.1.7. Ancestor Keyboard Phase Extension

Status: APPROVED by Gabriel on2026-10-29: “Approve scoped keyboard helper.” Exact target: `CAT.toggle-button.G01` caller/ancestor key phases. This is an explicit native equivalent for an ancestor that participates in the toggle group's key path. It adds no View, proxy ref or hidden target. The original container ref, physical same-window containment, current binding/epoch/policy revision and retained native/Fabric ancestry admit each delivery. The existing NativeFocusView API keeps its current contract; the new helper applies only to the owned group's dispatch path.

The private group adapter must run registered ancestor capture, internal toolbar capture, target and ancestor bubble in their original order. Capture stopPropagation prevents later phases. Capture preventDefault alone does not suppress toolbar arrow focus; the toolbar still stops propagation and prevents the arrow default. For Tab, edge focus occurs and the original native default remains allowed only if no earlier callback prevented it. Home/End remain unhandled by the toolbar. Deliver current callbacks against original native refs/events, preserve keyup/cancel/lifecycle and retire stale work. Do not call consumer selection/press handlers to simulate a key result. The complete current public/source/scene/native-compiler/consumer proof in3.5.3.1.6 remains mandatory before adoption.

Approved call site; implementation and public adoption remain uncompleted:

```tsx
<NativeToggleButtonGroupKeyboardScope containerRef={parentRef} onKeyDownCapture={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
  <NativeFocusView ref={parentRef}>
    <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label="Formatting">{/* original toggles */}</ToggleButtonGroup>
  </NativeFocusView>
</NativeToggleButtonGroupKeyboardScope>
```

Approval extends only the source public/helper and scoped phase-transport boundary stated here. Approved public boundary:

```ts
export type TNativePressEvent = GestureResponderEvent | TNativeKeyboardEvent
export type TNativeKeyboardData = Readonly<{
  kind: "keyboard"
  key: string
  nativeCode: number
  characters: string
  phase: "down" | "up"
  repeat: boolean
  shiftKey: boolean
  altKey: boolean
  ctrlKey: boolean
  metaKey: boolean
  capsLock: boolean
  nativeModifierData: string
  nativeDefaultHandled: boolean
}>
export type TNativeKeyboardEvent = NativeSyntheticEvent<TNativeKeyboardData>
export const NativeFocusView: NativeViewComponentWithActualViewRef
export const focusNativeTarget: (target: View | TextInput | null) => boolean
export const blurNativeTarget: (target: View | TextInput | null) => boolean
```

The boolean helper result means request admission, not completed focus; completion is proven by the native event/target. The sketch's NativeViewComponentWithActualViewRef denotes the ordinary typed View-props/ref boundary, not a new opaque imperative handle. Native key scope/description/viewport/scroll facades remain private. This is a new native-equivalent contract: existing measurement/editor refs and caller state remain stable, while programmatic non-text focus and keyboard press events gain explicit APIs. The main cost is owning and validating a small two-platform native transport layer and shipping its native source inputs.

Alternative for owner consideration: use exact1.2.1 only as a patched low-level backend, with an explicit consumer patch policy, a complete Meta/key schema patch, Codon-owned press/lease/description/viewport/scroll adapters and actual refs instead of the upstream Proxy/HOCs. This would add a new native peer/dev/showcase dependency plus patch-distribution obligations, and still needs the same required native proof. It is not approved or a fallback to adopt silently. A flag-only route or unmodified dependency does not satisfy the demonstrated two-platform contracts. Prefer the source-owned adapter to keep those semantics, source ownership and existing pins under one implementation.

#### 3.5.22. Native Activation And Release Contract

Status: **Approved by Gabriel on 2026-10-18: “Approve activation/release contract.” Source, public declarations, consumer and matching Release linkage pass at 17b7882; installed acceptance remains OPEN.** Metadata key: `DEC.native-activation.01`. The approved3.5.21 event union has touch and keyboard arms. A further primary-source audit finds that pinned Android ViewGroupClickEvent produces an empty native data map, while iOS RCTViewComponentView exposes a separate accessibilityActivate/onAccessibilityTap route. Neither source establishes a genuine touch-coordinate payload for every native activation. Canonical React Aria3.48 usePress handles virtual activation through semantic start/change, up, end/change and one action; its held-pointer and held-keyboard branches avoid duplicate activation. Physical spoken output remains deferred, but truthful public event typing and native binding remain mandatory3.1.1–3.1.3/3.1.7–3.1.8 capabilities.

Approved public correction, under the existing source-owned backend and without dependencies or SDK flags:

```ts
export const NATIVE_ACTIVATION_SOURCES = ["android-click", "ios-accessibility-activate"] as const
export type TNativeActivationSource = (typeof NATIVE_ACTIVATION_SOURCES)[number]
export type TNativeInteractionEvent = GestureResponderEvent | TNativeKeyboardEvent
export type TNativeActivationData = Readonly<{
  kind: "activation"
  target: number
  source: TNativeActivationSource
  observedAt: number
}>
export type TNativeActivationEvent = NativeSyntheticEvent<TNativeActivationData>
export type TNativePressEvent = TNativeInteractionEvent | TNativeActivationEvent
```

observedAt is the native callback-observation clock, not an invented hardware-input timestamp. Activation has no touch coordinates, key codes or fabricated native down/up. Existing native pointer/key event objects remain unchanged. onPress plus semantic onPressStart/onPressEnd and the canonical onPressUp equivalent admit the truthful three-arm event; raw onPressIn/onPressOut keep the existing touch-or-keyboard interaction type. Callers inspecting kind narrow keyboard versus activation explicitly, then inspect actual touch fields only in the touch arm. Existing source callers, executable declarations and usage examples must migrate coherently rather than casting activation to GestureResponderEvent.

A private codegen/native activation record binds the actual Android click or iOS accessibility-activation callback, with native owner/window/lifetime admission and one-action delivery. Idle activation follows canonical semantic start → change(true) → up → end → change(false) → action using the original activation record; a held pointer completes once and a held keyboard does not gain a duplicate virtual action. Preserve separately forwarded SDK accessibility callbacks and their original events. Raw press-in/out callbacks are not manufactured for a callback that supplied no physical down/up. Real touch/key release supplies semantic onPressUp only for the current admitted, uncancelled cycle. Disabled/pending, replacement/unmount, callback changes and window loss retain3.5.21's guards and actual native default-handling policy. Controlled values, actual refs, palette, geometry and slots remain unchanged.

Verify original native record identity/fields, absence of fictitious coordinates, exact semantic/raw callback order, touch/keyboard preservation, long-press/repeat/re-entry, owner vetoes and all lifetime/guard combinations. Public positive/negative fixtures must prove each arm and press-up contract. Fresh outside-workspace archive/declaration/Metro/native products remain required; actual simulator/emulator activation/default/lifetime cases cannot be replaced with source injection or physical-lane deferral. This decision extends the earlier approved public event API and now has the required owner review under AGENTS.md. The source increment binds Android native click and iOS accessibilityActivate, forwards SDK accessibility callbacks separately and implements semantic release. It is recorded at a separate logical boundary in [3.31.12](experiments.md#33112-native-activation-and-release), retaining every applicable acceptance cell; CP-46 supplies matching fresh consumer/Release linkage at 17b7882, while 110 explicit native activation/release cells and all actual installed proof remain OPEN.

Status: **Approved directly by Gabriel for the complete pointer-default amendment and all six construction/proof parts below.** The pinned Menu mouse-grace hook suppresses parent pointer interaction and prevents pointer-down defaults while the pointer travels toward an open submenu. The current native window-pointer transport is expressly passive and observes dispatch after capturing its hit path; the owned Android pressable also enables actual native clicks/focus. An asynchronous JavaScript focus/action veto is therefore insufficient evidence for the required native default-prevention contract. This is an inspected source/control-flow discrepancy, not an executed native failure or permission to change the existing observer's default path. Preserve the passive motion transport and all public pointer/keyboard/activation events. ##### 3.5.54.12. Original Editor Keyboard Defaults Decision

Status: **Approved in full by Gabriel on2026-10-22, including all eight parts, the bounded prototype, shared private phase/default/ack APIs and complete adoption only after positive proof.** The existing3.5.54.11 full-family approval remains effective. - **3.5.54.12.1. Exact callback/phase surface.** Add the missing original-editor autofocus and full down/up/cancel callback surface within the approved family receiver. Preserve original target/current original ref, key/code/native code, location, modifiers, composition, repeat, timestamp and monotonic native event identity. No reconstructed press, cloned callback event, public event-method patch or duplicate key stream is permitted. Callback-only changes preserve the current binding; editor/window/Activity/descriptor replacement retires it.
- **3.5.54.12.2. Separate synchronous default owner.** Prototype a private exact-original-editor keyboard-default registration alongside the passive observer, using the pinned Fabric synchronous event facilities and a small private blocking acknowledgement module. Android decides within the existing original dispatchKeyEvent call before its single super dispatch. UIKit must prove public press/gesture arbitration on the exact original editor before its default, with a separate owned recognizer rather than changing the passive observer. The original JavaScript event's preventDefault/isDefaultPrevented result is acknowledged while that exact native dispatch is still live; source internal ComboBox behavior runs before the caller callback in the observed source order. Existing built-in navigation joins this owner so it cannot suppress or execute the same default twice.
- **3.5.54.12.3. Preserve the original editor and default.** A declined veto or no callback lets the original SDK event continue once. An admitted veto prevents that exact original default. No event replay, synthetic key, input replacement/subclass/proxy, input/editor/key delegate patch, text/value/selection/composition write, method swizzle, application-window replacement/interposition, new private getter/field, SDK flag, dependency/pin, signing or service change is approved. If UIKit's public arbitration cannot meet these constraints, the prototype fails and dependent adoption stops with that evidence; no observational callback or declarative approximation silently substitutes for the source veto capability.
- **3.5.54.12.4. Admission and settlement.** The acknowledgement must match one current owner, original editor identity, descriptor/binding, native document/window/epoch, event ID and phase on its original dispatch stack. Stale/foreign/duplicate/late acknowledgements cannot veto a later event. Missing/failed acknowledgements preserve the original platform default once and report a non-success disposition. Exceptions and nested/reentrant requests settle once without leaving a window or editor captured. No persisted promise, held SDK event or later callback can acquire default authority. Required actual SDK verdicts.** Original hardware-key delivery must show allowed editing once, vetoed editing absent, retained original text/selection/composition and original ref/focus, down/up/repeat/cancel ordering, source open/default/caller order, modifiers, unhandled keys, callback replacement, unmount, Activity/window retirement, stale/foreign/duplicate rejection and accessor/handler cleanup. ### 3.6. LinearProgress And Meter Contract

Status: **Approved by Gabriel on 2026-10-17 for paired implementation, tests, showcase, documentation and logical commits.** The audit covers both complete component/helper/CSS/root-suite/index files and the pinned React Aria ProgressBar/Meter render props, range clamping and formatting behavior. These display-only components need no text editor, overlay, collection, new runtime or new theme role. Counter is excluded because it additionally depends on CircularProgress.

| Surface                               | Approved native contract / verification                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ownership and range                   | Required `value: number`; optional `minValue`/`maxValue` default to 0/100. Values remain caller-owned, including zero and negatives; no local/default value or change callback. Require finite values/bounds and `maxValue > minValue`, clamp presentation to bounds and calculate percentage from the entire range. Reject invalid ranges explicitly rather than emit NaN geometry.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Progress versus meter                 | `LinearProgress` describes task progress and alone accepts `isIndeterminate`. `Meter` describes a measurement and has no indeterminate state. Both expose a real native View ref. Root roles/value semantics are component-owned; native `role="meter"` on iOS and progressbar compatibility on Android are the meter equivalents, subject to later installed/screen-reader acceptance.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Accessible name and value             | Require nonempty `accessibilityLabel` or `aria-label`, with the existing native spelling taking precedence. Use native accessibility range/value text, not DOM label associations. Preserve `valueLabel` as an optional caller-authored string (including empty); otherwise format with existing Intl support, `formatOptions` and an explicit optional `locale`. Default formatting is percentage; non-percent formatting uses the bounded numeric value. Formatting/Intl remains host-owned with no bootstrap or dependency change. Indeterminate progress omits numeric value/text. |
| Dimensions, orientation and direction | Root defaults to 150 × 10 logical units horizontally or 10 × 150 vertically, with a filling track. Retain `height`/`width` as native dimensions, `orientation` horizontal/vertical and `direction` left/right/up/down. Horizontal defaults right; vertical defaults up; directions on the other axis have no effect, matching web behavior. Test zero, percentage dimensions, rerenders and direction/orientation changes without mirrored value state.                                                                                                                                |
| Colors, geometry and elevation        | Retain `barColor`, `trackColor`, `order`, independent `barGeometry`/`trackGeometry` and `raised`. Use existing native ColorValue validation, semantic selected/background/border roles, action backgrounds, radius tokens and established native shadow/elevation. Custom colors override order. No palette or theme-contract edits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Customization                         | Retain separate `customStyles`, `customTrackStyles` and `customBarStyles` native style slots. Root precedence remains computed → customStyles → final `style`; a style callback receives percentage/value text (plus indeterminate state only on progress) and the post-custom `defaultStyle`. Track/bar styles override their computed presentation. Preserve native identity/layout props and test that wrapper props do not leak to host views.                                                                                                                                     |
| Motion and unknown progress           | Use the existing core RN Animated capability for bounded 250 ms determinate transitions, respecting Reduce Motion and stopping obsolete/unmounted animations. The numeric accessibility value and callback state reflect current controlled props immediately. Indeterminate progress uses a decorative core ActivityIndicator with no invented numeric progress; it is not exposed as a second accessibility target. No Motion/React Aria/native animation dependency is added.                                                                                                       |
| Explicit native equivalents           | DOM class names, browser refs/events/form associations, React Aria slot context and arbitrary ReactNode value labels are not native APIs. These are documented substitutions, not silent parity claims. These wrappers own their track/bar children as the canonical web wrappers do. Keep native accessibility speech, measured layout, motion and platform rendering as outstanding installed/device evidence.                                                                                                                                                                       |

The complete root web suites each contain 13 cases covering rendering, semantic default color, dimensions, explicit colors, three geometries, five orders/numbered palette roles, raised state, direction, orientation, three style slots, final override precedence and wrapper prop consumption. Map every assertion to native behavior; add inherited-contract tests for bounded ranges/negative and zero values, formatting/value labels, progress-only indeterminacy, accessible names/owned roles, refs/native forwarding, theme changes, callback defaultStyle, animation cleanup and reduced motion. Type tests accept native dimensions/styles/refs and reject unsupported ownership/DOM/indeterminate-meter surfaces. Use focused Jest suites, native contract typecheck/build and showcase composition tests; record installed iOS/Android/physical proof as pending instead of certifying it through mocks.

<a id="ownership-and-accepted-contracts"></a>

## 4. Ownership And Accepted Contracts

`packages/react` owns canonical React source, theme CSS and registry definitions; `packages/react-native` owns shared TypeScript/TSX native components, typed native theme and the approved3.5.21 source-owned Objective-C++/Java interaction adapter. `apps/native-showcase` owns its generic Expo consumer and app-only Intl bootstrap. `apps/web` does not own canonical registry source or artifact generation. `packages/CLI` owns current source-distribution CLI behavior; `apps/docs` owns durable documentation. Sibling repositories remain separate; this work does not edit Wavemap or Waveguide.

Controlled values remain authoritative, including false, zero, empty string/array and contract-defined null. Undefined alone selects the documented uncontrolled/default path. Preserve event-count protection, existing callback/veto semantics, native refs and style precedence. Do not add effect-driven mirrors, uncontrolled fallback or event suppression to make an automated text test pass. Component [types](../../packages/react-native/src/index.ts), focused suites and the curated [native package reference](../../apps/docs/src/content/docs/packages/react-native.md) own the implemented API; past proposal text does not authorize additional APIs.

| Boundary                  | Accepted decision and remaining limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Theme and style           | Keep the hand-authored palette, semantic roles, user scaling, computed → customStyles → final style precedence and owned text context. No NativeWind or new styling runtime. Colocated typed calibration is preferred when a substantive edit benefits; no broad cleanup is authorized.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Text/Button               | Native targets, refs, labels, scaling, interaction guards and foreground ownership replace DOM/CSS mechanics; closer owner visual and physical evidence remain separate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Basic controls            | Controlled/default ownership and native disabled/read-only/pending guards remain at activation. Input delegates controlled native synchronization to RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Select/ListBoxItem        | One typed key/null, independent open ownership, caller filtering/collections and safe-area full-screen presentation; missing selection retention is accepted. The bounded 32-attempt positioning algorithm requires actual measurement progress and full-row visibility.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| TextArea/Radio/RadioGroup | Preserve native multiline/submit/name behavior and required group ownership, nullable selection and same-value suppression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| NumberInput               | Keep raw draft separate from nullable committed numeric value, bounded decimal model, final native-event publication, bounds/precision/step guards and explicit child prop ownership. App consumers prepare Intl before native barrel import.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Modal/AlertDialog         | Caller-controlled ownership, one host/leaf chain, context/draft retention, safe-area/keyboard/window geometry and callback-before-close semantics; public nesting and broader compositions retain their acceptance gates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| PlaceholderText/ComboBox  | Single typed selection key/null, independent value/query/open axes, caller-filtered readonly async items, guarded rows, owned refs and distinct root/input/button/group/list slots. Default full-screen presentation is accepted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Deferred web capabilities | Anchored/inline placement, alternate triggers, default collections/filtering/collation, committed custom free text, multiple selection, DOM form/class/portal behavior and web focus wrapping need explicit native equivalents or a documented exclusion before parity certification. No capability is silently removed from the catalogue.                                                                                                                  |
| React source distribution | Keep manifest/graph/CSS ownership, advisory CLI findings, install/update/diff/remove safety and existing proof packets. Curated [registry contracts](../../apps/docs/src/content/docs/registry/contracts.md), [ingest](../../apps/docs/src/content/docs/registry/ingest.md) and [CLI lifecycle](../../apps/docs/src/content/docs/cli/consumer-lifecycle.md) own settled behavior. SourceRef strings in immutable proof packets remain historical provenance. |

<a id="verification-gaps"></a>

## 7. Verification Gaps

Canonical web React component contracts are the minimum native verification baseline. Verify public behavior, callbacks, refs, labels, dimensions/geometry/size, focus/validation, named slots and override precedence, then add native keyboard/window/accessibility proof. Test counts, mocks and a passing repeated native typing case cannot certify coverage parity.

| Canonical web assertion                                         | Current native evidence                                                                                                                             | Remaining verification / disposition                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Placeholder b11/italic/placeholder color/default alignment      | Direct native leaf assertions, provider overrides, scaling and Text inheritance boundary                                                            | Source tier covered; installed family acceptance incomplete.                                                                        |
| Placeholder center alignment, element type, custom class/styles | Center alignment and native style precedence tested; native ref/labels/events tested                                                                | DOM classes/elements follow the accepted native Text equivalent/exception; no DOM emulation.                                        |
| ComboBox renders                                                | Source outcome cases render trigger/query/list/Close                                                                                                | First installed typing gate failed; receipt retains it.                                                                             |
| Height and width props                                          | Direct iOS/Android default minima, authored height/width, percentage/auto dimensions and computed/custom/final dimension precedence                 | Source tier covered; installed geometry and touch-target acceptance remain separate.                                                |
| Color prop                                                      | Isolated foreground propagation to summary/query/default glyph; button foreground override remains local to owned summary/icon                      | Source tier covered; installed color/visual review remains separate.                                                                |
| Rounded/round/orthogonal geometry                               | All three radii asserted on summary/query groups, trigger and query input                                                                           | Source tier covered; installed geometry remains separate.                                                                           |
| Small/medium/large text size                                    | All three summary/query sizes asserted, with provider font-size changes on the mounted component                                                    | Source tier covered; native large-text layout/scaling acceptance remains separate.                                                  |
| enableFocusStyle and offsetFocusRing                            | Trigger/query focus and blur drive actual group styles; style opt-out and zero/default offsets asserted                                             | Source tier covered with simulated events; native focus/keyboard behavior remains separate.                                         |
| Disabled                                                        | Repeated opening/editing/result guards and controlled takeover tested                                                                               | Installed disabled behavior remains pending for this family.                                                                        |
| isOpen                                                          | Three authoritative axes, repeated vetoes and programmatic owner transitions tested                                                                 | Installed owner/open/action matrix remains pending.                                                                                 |
| Error, warning, success borders and error priority              | Isolated states, warning-over-success/error priority and removal back to baseline asserted on both groups                                           | Source tier covered; installed visual states remain separate.                                                                       |
| Root, input, group and button style slots                       | Each root/input/button/group/list slot independently changes rendered output; summary-button foreground and existing final root precedence asserted | Source tier covered; no additional slots or styling API introduced.                                                                 |
| Default/custom icon                                             | Default chevron geometry and open/closed rotation, authored replacement and explicit null override asserted                                         | Source tier covered through decorative host-node inspection; pixel/physical review remains separate.                                |
| className/style retain computed root styles                     | Native customStyles/final style callback precedence and post-custom defaultStyle tested                                                             | Class plumbing is an explicit native exception; preserve equivalent native style precedence tests.                                  |
| Wrapper props do not leak to root                               | Consumed wrapper props absent on native root; native identity/layout/pointer/collapsable props forward directly                                     | Source tier covered; unsupported public surfaces remain rejected by existing types.                                                 |
| Custom internal labels and empty copy                           | Separate native trigger/query/Close labels, aliases, invalid-name guards and custom empty text tested                                               | Names deliberately match native targets rather than a DOM group/Popover; installed speech/localization acceptance remains separate. |

The focused [ComboBox suite](../../packages/react-native/src/components/ComboBox/__tests__/ComboBox.test.tsx) now passes 55 cases, including 24 added customization cases. This closes the listed source-assertion debt without production changes. Rendered host styles/props, simulated focus events and mocked platform defaults do not prove actual layout, keyboard delivery or physical accessibility. [The evidence companion](experiments.md#5-combobox-customization-coverage) records the exact verification tier.

Full ComboBox installed acceptance still needs first result activation after focused typing, keyboard-active Close/Back, nested context/draft/theme, disabled/owner-veto behavior, large text/rotation/removal and both platform gates. TagComboBox/Table/date leaves are not promoted by diagnostic success. Physical speech/localization/touch/ARM evidence remains distinct.

<a id="rn-text-01-bounded-investigation"></a>

## 8. RN-TEXT-01 Bounded Investigation

Gabriel authorizes this run on 2026-10-16 with logical commits and preserved controlled values, pins and palette. Compare the prior first raw N-only failure against its passing warm repeat before any production repair. First inspect the complete event timelines and pinned RN JS/Fabric/UITextField adapter source; key callbacks are proposal-path observations, not proof of applied text.

The frozen comparison permits at most two new raw attempts after real callback validation: first after guest boot and one warm application restart. Keep the frozen Release application, one unpaced Native query text call, initially empty controlled query and keyboard/correction defaults. A private inspector variant may pause only after attaching its immutable focused verdict so a bounded read-only LLDB snapshot can compare UIKit marked/selected text and RN/delegate state. Label observer timing explicitly; no breakpoint, setter, swizzle, native production change or typing intervention is permitted during the burst. A post-verdict snapshot cannot reconstruct the full mutation sequence.

The continuation authorized on 2026-10-16 repairs and validates XCTest transport in one run capped at 60 minutes, with at most three repair preflights, one per-user simulator-service recycle while all guests are stopped and one fresh guest on the existing runtime if needed. Replay frozen products directly through their xctestrun, keep installer/PID observations optional and require the actual Transport 1 callback attachment, not merely process launch or a passing controller. Validate the selected observer warm and after guest shutdown/reboot before the two raw cases. Keep native-session progress, fixed silence/total caps, failed assertions and incomplete results. A successful repair is a logical commit boundary before comparison findings.

The preceding source/trace investigation completed without a native extension: two preflights failed to reach methods after one retained-guest recovery, yielding zero new raw attempts or snapshots. Preserve that outcome in [the existing experiment section](experiments.md#9-current-raw-firstwarm-investigation); it does not invalidate the earlier successful transport or failed/passing raw traces. Do not erase guests, reset security/keyboard preferences, expand case order/correction/pacing, rerun Input/ComboBox, change production synchronization or dependencies, publish upstream, or sign for iPhone. Restore/stop task guests and retain partial results if this continuation reaches its bound.

The continuation completes its native budget with one service recycle, one fresh same-runtime guest and three repair preflights. Three callback passes in the retained guest are followed by a raw controller startup regression before any method or typing; they do not prove general transport stability. The final fresh-guest configuration passes callback validation first/warm/reboot, then immediately completes exactly two raw methods. First raw shows full native-observed text while controlled channels remain Na; warm raw agrees on the corrupted Na texttive query. Both remain focused with keyboard active and fail the intended phrase. Neither bounded post-verdict LLDB attempt returns native state. The private scheme does not remove Xcode's internal debugger-wait flag, and no unique recovery cause is claimed. See [the comparison and limits](experiments.md#9-current-raw-firstwarm-investigation). Stop here with RN-TEXT-01 open; native change-publication, controlled-write and selection/composition evidence is still required before a production remedy. All task guests are stopped, frozen identities and prior seals are verified, and signing remains deferred.

The subsequent LLDB/native-trace continuation is authorized on 2026-10-16, capped at 60 minutes with at most two task-owned host-probe attachments, an initial three simulator attachments and two instrumented raw methods at most. After automatic approval review rejects an over-budget replay, Gabriel explicitly approves one additional capped attachment/harness replay to correct the agent-authored expression compiler error after successful attach/import; no earlier typing ran and the original 60-minute deadline stays fixed. Keep the same retained guest, frozen app/source/pins/palette and deferred iPhone signing; no security reset, guest erase or production repair is included. Validate real attach/register-memory read/detach/resume before tracing. The current native-tracing request permits bounded auto-continue breakpoints in a separately labeled observer condition, superseding the preceding frozen comparison's prohibition for this instrumented phase only. A private XCTest gate may wait before the unchanged unpaced typing call; record scheduling effects and preserve original focused assertions. The debugger may read native event counters, flags, proposal arguments and controlled-write arguments, but may not set values, patch guard flags or change keyboard defaults. Keep attach/symbol-load/evaluation failures distinct. Commit validated session support and then the trace findings at logical boundaries; keep evidence in the existing experiment section.

The LLDB continuation stops with real simulator attach/register-memory read/detach/resume proof and one corrected private preflight callback pass, but without a live native mutation trace. Attachment03 reaches UIKit import and then fails on the agent's metadata-expression compilation; its corrected wrapper passes offline syntax checks. The single approved final replay fails during application launch before the pretyping gate, so it consumes no fourth attachment and performs no typing. Actual totals are three simulator attachments, three gated raw invocations and zero native breakpoint events or focused text verdicts. [The evidence companion](experiments.md#10-lldb-attachment-and-native-trace) preserves these distinct outcomes. The native run ends within its original bound, all task guests stop and frozen identities remain unchanged. RN-TEXT-01 and the frozen comparison remain open. The next prerequisite is dependable no-editor startup plus a minimal successful live metadata read; the unvalidated larger probe must not trigger another implicit replay or production workaround.

The next startup/minimal-metadata continuation is authorized on 2026-10-16 with logical commits and a 45-minute bound: at most three no-editor startup validations, one retained-guest reboot, two simulator debugger attachments and one instrumented raw invocation after prerequisites pass. A private observer may require and activate a host-prelaunched frozen app instead of terminating/launching it through XCTest; callback proof also requires the same owned PID/birth/executable identity before and after the method. Require at least two actual callback passes, including one after reboot, then a minimal live metadata read before tracing. Preserve failed attempts and distinct startup/observer conditions. No new guest, service/security reset, app rebuild, keyboard/default/pacing change, production repair or iPhone signing is included. Commit validated startup support separately from the live-probe/trace findings, then stop and seal within the fixed bound.

The startup/minimal-metadata continuation ends without a validated repair: one capped host-prelaunch attempt times out before XCTest begins, and later process presence does not prove readiness. Actual counts are zero callback validations, zero debugger attachments, zero live metadata probes and zero typing. The final read-only process observation exceeds the stated deadline by about two minutes; record that overrun rather than treating it as an authorized extension. Only cleanup follows. ## 9. Working And Evidence Rules

Use `feature/<description>` branches unless Gabriel explicitly chooses another name. Commit one coherent library step at a natural boundary: audited contracts, component source/tests, then maintained consumer examples/reference and evidence. Diagnostic work requires its own explicit scope; the active delivery goal excludes further XCTest startup investigation. Do not generate a new roadmap, pass/receipt pair or duplicate status table per timeout. Keep current work here and experiment details in experiments.md. Raw command logs, captures, source/binary hashes and private harnesses remain in evidence packets; stable explanations graduate into curated docs.

Keep every section heading below the document title in decimal hierarchy (`## 1.`, `### 1.1.`, `#### 1.1.1.`). Use the numbered rubric, scenario and profile references in roadmap prose and matrix labels; stable evidence codes are metadata only. Before each planning commit, verify sequential heading numbers, contents targets, local section links and legacy anchors in both planning files.

Use the narrowest meaningful verification: affected fixture/helper checks, strict native-consumer types where changed, native preflight/raw verdicts, frozen source/archive/installed identities, targeted planning Markdown/link checks, docs build where curated pages change, normal commit hooks and git diff --check. Do not rebuild unchanged production code or rerun broad suites simply to fill a receipt. Preserve local Git identity, hooks, failed native assertions and exact observer revisions. Branch pushes and library pull requests are authorized under §9.1; merge, unrelated report sending and publication remain unauthorized.

Never execute/import helpers inside a SEALED packet or write beneath it. Copy required helpers to a fresh root and rewrite roots before use. Verify inherited manifests as data; retain the two known pre-seal unlisted bytecode files in the oldest packet. New native inspection must be labeled separately from unchanged application identity. Planning migration uses local Git revision db54a8a for complete former documents and preserves provenance strings rather than rewriting historical evidence. See the [migration lookup](experiments.md#12-historical-document-lookup).
